minutes.headline: School Committee approved the ESSER spending priorities and ratified a custodial contract
minutes.summary: After a short executive session on union negotiations, the committee approved handbooks, a carry-forward list of open purchase orders, a three-year custodial agreement, a textbook disposal, the ESSER priorities plan with its job postings, and a corrected FY22 calendar. Most of the meeting was the superintendent and business manager presenting survey results and how ESSER II, ESSER III and other grants would fund staffing.

attendees.role: middle school principal and interim high school principal

votes.motion: Enter executive session for strategy in preparation for negotiations with union personnel
Approve the middle school and high school handbooks
Approve the carry forward list of purchase orders
Accept and ratify the custodial union memorandum of agreement
Approve the declaration of excess for LMHS textbooks
Approve the ESSER priorities and the associated job postings

budget_items.what_was_said: Money for Chromebooks was encumbered in one fiscal year and received in another during COVID, as an example of why purchase orders carry forward.
The business manager asked the committee to approve the list of open purchase orders to carry into next year, noting it will likely shrink before year end.
A three-year custodial contract has cost-of-living increases and a retro payment, with a cost given for each fiscal year.
figures_as_heard: fourteen thousand seven hundred and seventy three dollars

budget_items.what_was_said: ESSER II must be spent by September 2023 and ESSER III by June 2024. A small after-school grant and a Student Opportunity Act grant were also received.
Percentages of the grant were allocated to social emotional, academic and operations, and the operations share covers retirement and insurance for grant-paid staff.
The business manager corrected the split across the three buckets, with operations coming down once guidance counselors were reclassified.
The superintendent said the total is spread over three years and goes quickly.
A committee member reported the town will receive two installments of federal recovery funds, decided by the town manager and select board.
The pay-as-you-go trash bag fee will rise on July 1 as haulers change.

decisions.decision: The next meeting will be August 18, with a workshop led by an outside facilitator.
The FY22 school calendar was corrected for an omitted October row, moving the last day of school a day earlier.

what_happened.line: The committee voted to approve the ESSER priorities and the job postings that go with them; the minutes record the vote as not audible.
The committee voted to accept and ratify the three-year custodial union memorandum of agreement; the outcome was not audible.
The committee voted on the carry-forward list of open purchase orders, which the business manager said will likely shrink before year end; the outcome was not audible.
The committee voted to approve a corrected 2021-2022 calendar, which moves the last day of school a day earlier after an omitted October row was fixed.
The committee also voted on the middle and high school handbooks and on declaring excess high school textbooks; the next meeting is August 18.

why_it_matters: ESSER is one-time federal money with spending deadlines in 2023 and 2024, so staff paid from it become a question for the town budget when the grants end.
The custodial agreement is a three-year commitment with cost-of-living increases, so it sets a cost for each of the next three school budgets.
